How I work

The same four moves on every project, whether the team is three people or thirty.

I

Understand

Sit with the people who use the product. Watch what they do before asking what they want.

II

Frame

Write the problem in one sentence the whole team can repeat, including the people who sign off budgets.

III

Shape

Sketch wide, prototype fast, and pick the simplest version that still solves the problem.

IV

Prove

Ship in stages, measure behaviour instead of opinions, and keep improving after launch.

I design the quiet parts of complex software: the dashboards, workflows and systems people rely on all day.

I am a senior UX designer with 5+ years across SaaS, B2B and B2C platforms. I began in mechanical engineering, designing in SOLIDWORKS and CATIA, which taught me to think in systems and to design with implementation in mind. At Kylas I led UX for two global enterprise CRM platforms. Today at Cognizant I work directly with clients on customer-facing web and mobile products.

I use AI tools such as Claude, Figma Make and ChatGPT to speed up research synthesis and prototyping, while keeping judgement, accessibility and user evidence at the centre of every decision.

How I collaborate

Design is a team sport. This is how I work with the people around me.

Product managers

I frame problems with them, tie design decisions to measurable business outcomes, and help estimate and plan design work.

In practice: shared problem statements, success metrics and estimates before work starts.

Engineers and QA

An engineering background means I design with implementation in mind. Tokens, component libraries and annotated specs keep handoff smooth.

In practice: agile delivery, with accessible features shipped on time.

Clients and stakeholders

I run discovery workshops, present design strategy in business terms and keep everyone aligned as scope changes.

In practice: workshops, written rationale and regular design reviews.
